key_insight: For type 2 diabetes phenotyping, RAG performance depended on embedding choice and prompting, with trade-offs between sensitivity, specificity, and token use.
clinical_relevance: Configurable RAG may support EHR cohort identification, but settings should reflect research priorities around missed cases versus false positives.
method: Processed 170,678 clinical notes from 275 ICD-screened patients using GPT-4o.
Tested seven embedding models and 350 embedding–chunk size–retrieval depth combinations on training data.
Evaluated eight optimized configurations with three prompts against ICD codes and institutional PheNorm.
evidence_signal: Across 24 test-set prompt–configuration combinations, RAG averaged 90.2% sensitivity, 79.1% specificity, and 92.0% F1; every combination exceeded ICD codes in PPV.
watch_item: Results from a small, ICD-screened cohort may not generalize to unscreened populations or other institutions.
paper_title: Systematic Benchmarking and Optimization of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for Clinical Phenotyping: A Type II Diabetes Case Study in an ICD-Screened Cohort
